title: The check-in kiosk
brief: Build a complete check-in screen. Read a day number and a room number, then print the three-line boarding information with exact labels and newlines.
input: Two integers: day (0–31), room (0–999).
output: Exactly: CODEX C / CHECK-IN, then Day: D, Room: R, Ready to code! (one line each).

tests.label: Example
tests.output:
CODEX C / CHECK-IN
Day: 2
Room: 17
Ready to code!

tests.label: Case 2
tests.output:
CODEX C / CHECK-IN
Day: 0
Room: 0
Ready to code!

tests.label: Case 3
tests.output:
CODEX C / CHECK-IN
Day: 31
Room: 999
Ready to code!

hints: Use one scanf to read both numbers.
Print each label exactly with printf.
Check spaces, capitalisation and the final newline.

title: The check-in kiosk: reserved seat
brief: Keep the check-in screen. Read a third number for the seat, and insert a Seat line before Ready to code!
input: Three integers: day (0–31), room (0–999), seat (0–999).
output: The same four lines, with Seat: S inserted before Ready to code!.

tests.label: Example
tests.output:
CODEX C / CHECK-IN
Day: 2
Room: 17
Seat: 4
Ready to code!

tests.label: Case 2
tests.output:
CODEX C / CHECK-IN
Day: 0
Room: 0
Seat: 0
Ready to code!

tests.label: Case 3
tests.output:
CODEX C / CHECK-IN
Day: 31
Room: 999
Seat: 100
Ready to code!

tests.label: Case 4
tests.output:
CODEX C / CHECK-IN
Day: 8
Room: 9
Seat: 7
Ready to code!

hints: Read three integers instead of two.
Keep the original output in the same order.
Insert only the new Seat: S line before the closing line.

title: The trip planner
brief: Read distance, speed, and the fare in cents per kilometre. Calculate the travel time in full hours and remaining minutes (truncated), and the cost in cents.
input: Three integers: distance 0–1000 km, speed 1–200 km/h, fare 0–100 cents/km.
output: travel=Hh Mm cost=Cc; minutes are distance*60/speed, truncated toward zero.
hints: First calculate the total number of travel minutes.
Use /60 and %60 to split the time.
Multiply distance by fare to obtain cents.

title: The trip planner: service charge
brief: Keep the travel time and cost; read a service-charge percentage and add the truncated service charge to produce the total.
input: The same three integers, then service-charge percentage 0–20.
output: travel=Hh Mm cost=Cc total=Tc; T=C+(C*percentage/100), with integer arithmetic.
hints: Keep the original time calculation.
Calculate the service charge with integer division.
Add it to cost; print both cost and total.

title: Campus access control
brief: Read age, badge status (0 or 1), and hour. A visitor enters only with a badge, at age 16 or older, from 08:00 through 19:59. If admitted, fee is 2 for under-18s, otherwise 5.
input: Three integers: age 0–100, badge 0/1, hour 0–23.
output: access=YES fee=F if allowed; otherwise access=NO fee=0.
hints: Combine badge, age and opening hours with &&.
Use if/else to choose the access branch.
Select the fee only after granting access.

title: Campus access: weekdays and categories
brief: Also read the weekday (1=Monday through 7=Sunday). Deny access on weekends; append the category YOUTH, ADULT, or CLOSED.
input: Four integers: age 0–100, badge 0/1, hour 0–23, weekday 1–7.
output: The same, then category=YOUTH, ADULT, or CLOSED.
hints: Add weekday <= 5 to the opening condition.
Keep the original fee decisions.
Use CLOSED when denied; otherwise choose the category from age.

title: The signal scanner
brief: Read N measurements without using arrays. Add the positive even values and count the negative values. Zero counts as neither.
input: N (1–25), then N integers in [-100,100].
hints: Use a for loop to read N numbers one by one.
Check value > 0 and value % 2 == 0.
Increase the negative counter only when value < 0.

title: The signal scanner: longest positive run
brief: Retain the two statistics and calculate the longest consecutive run of strictly positive values using the same single pass (still no arrays).
input: Same input as the original challenge.
hints: Maintain a current positive run and a maximum.
Reset current run on a nonpositive number.
Update maximum after every positive value.

title: Sensor array audit
brief: Store N readings in a one-dimensional array. Find the minimum, maximum, and zero-based index of the first maximum (keep the first index when tied).
input: N (1–20), then N integers in [-100,100].
hints: Read all values into an int array.
Initialise min/max from the first element.
Use > (not >=) when updating the maximum's index.

title: Sensor array: values above average
brief: Keep those results, compute the integer average (C truncation toward zero) and count how many readings are strictly above that average.
input: Same input as the original challenge.
hints: Accumulate a sum while reading the array.
Divide by N using integer division.
Make another pass to count values greater than that average.

title: The grade calculator
brief: Create clampScore(int) and average3(int,int,int). Clamp each of three raw scores to 0–100, calculate their integer mean, and classify PASS when mean >= 50.
input: Three integers in [-20,120].
hints: Implement clampScore using if conditions.
Apply clampScore to every input before averaging.
Use integer division by three; compare mean with 50.

title: The grade calculator: median
brief: Keep the mean and classification, but also write a reusable median3(int,int,int) function operating on the three clamped scores.
input: Same three integers in [-20,120].
hints: The three values are already clamped.
The median is the middle value after comparing three numbers.
Use a dedicated median3 function and preserve the original result.

title: Coordinate workshop
brief: Use pointer parameters in swap(int*,int*) and shift(int*,int). Order two coordinates from low to high, then add a delta to each.
input: Three integers: coordinate a, coordinate b, delta; each in [-100,100].
output: a=A b=B after ordering then shifting.
hints: Define swap with two int* parameters.
Compare the variables and swap through their addresses.
Shift the ordered values by passing their addresses too.

title: Coordinate workshop: three values
brief: Extend the workshop to three coordinates. Order all three through pointer-based swaps and shift all three. Print the span between highest and lowest.
input: Four integers: coordinates a,b,c and delta, each in [-100,100].
output: a=A b=B c=C span=S after ordering then shifting.
hints: Use repeated pairwise swaps to order three values.
Shift every ordered value via shift(int*,int).
The span is c-a after sorting (it does not depend on delta).

title: The password inspector
brief: Read one ASCII token (letters and digits), at most 39 characters. Without string.h, count its length, its vowels (A/E/I/O/U, any case), and its digits.
input: One nonempty ASCII alphanumeric token of length 1–39.
hints: Read the token with scanf("%39s", text).
Walk until the null character is reached.
Use comparisons for digits and vowels in either case.

title: Password inspector: repeated characters
brief: Keep the inspection and add the length of the longest consecutive run of identical characters (case-sensitive).
input: Same token, length 1–39.
hints: Keep a counter for repeated adjacent characters.
Reset the counter when the current character changes.
Track the maximum; a one-character word has a run of 1.

title: The parcel dispatcher
brief: Declare a Parcel structure with id and weight. Read N parcels; choose the heaviest, breaking ties by smallest id. Store the records in an array of structures.
input: N (1–10), then N pairs: positive id (1–999), weight (0–100).
hints: Represent each parcel as a struct and create an array.
Remember the index of the best parcel seen so far.
Use a second comparison to break weight ties by id.

title: Parcel dispatcher: priority delivery
brief: Extend Parcel with a priority field. Choose the parcel with highest priority; break ties by highest weight, then smallest id.
input: N (1–10), then N triples: id (1–999), weight (0–100), priority (0–3).
hints: Add the priority member to the structure.
Compare priority before comparing weight.
Use id to break the final tie consistently.

title: The growing gradebook
brief: Allocate space for N grades using malloc, read the values into dynamic storage, compute sum/min/max, and release the allocation.
input: N (1–20), followed by N integers in [-100,100].
hints: Allocate N integers with malloc and check for NULL.
Read each value into the allocated array.
Find sum/min/max, then free exactly once.

title: Gradebook: resize safely
brief: After reading the first N grades, read M more and resize the same allocation using realloc. Compute the statistics over all N+M values.
input: N (1–20), N integers, then M (1–10) and M more integers. Total N+M <= 30.
output: count=N sum=S min=A max=B, with N equal to total number of grades.
hints: Read M after the first N elements.
Store realloc's result in a temporary pointer and check it.
Fill new positions and compute statistics over all N+M elements.

title: The statistics module
brief: Create stats.h and stats.c with guarded declarations for min3 and max3. Read three integers in main.c, call the functions from the other file, and display their results.
input: Three integers in [-100,100].

starter.stats.c:
#include "stats.h"
// TODO: implement the helper functions here.

hints: Declare prototypes inside the stats.h include guard.
Define the helpers in stats.c and include stats.h there.
Compile main.c and stats.c together; call from main.

title: Statistics module: a complete report
brief: Keep the separate files. Add mean3 and spread3 to the module, declare them in the header, and use them in the final report (integer average).
input: The same three integers.

starter.stats.c:
#include "stats.h"
// TODO: implement the helper functions here.

hints: Add mean3 and spread3 prototypes to the header.
Implement mean3 with integer division and spread3 using min3/max3.
Update main.c without duplicating the module's logic.

title: The reproducible dice contest
brief: Use state=(state*5+1)%97 and roll=state%6+1 (do NOT use rand). From seed and N rolls, report the sum and the number of rolls that were six.
hints: Start from the input seed.
Update state with %97 before each roll.
Sum all faces and separately count rolls equal to six.

title: Dice contest: streak tracking
brief: Keep the same simulated sequence. Also report its first face and the longest consecutive streak of exactly the same face.
input: Same seed (0–96) and N (1–30).
hints: Save the first roll when i==0.
Compare each face with the previous one.
Reset the run on a different face and keep the maximum.

title: The saved ledger
brief: Read N integers and save them to numbers.txt, one per line. Close and reopen the file; compute the sum and number of strictly positive values from the saved file.
input: N (1–20), followed by N integers in [-100,100].
hints: Open numbers.txt with fopen(...,"w") and write N lines.
Close the write handle before opening for reading.
Use fscanf on the file, not on stdin, to build the report.

title: The saved ledger: positive report
brief: While reopening numbers.txt, copy positive values to positives.txt. Close and reopen positives.txt to calculate the sum of positive values for the extended report.
input: Same input as the original challenge.
hints: Create positives.txt while reading numbers.txt.
Only copy values > 0; close both files.
Reopen positives.txt and sum its values with fscanf.

title: The recursive digit detective
brief: Without loops, implement recursive digitCount(n) and digitSum(n). Count zero as one digit. Read a nonnegative integer and print both results.
input: One integer N in [0,999999999].
hints: digitCount has base case n < 10.
digitSum has base case n < 10.
For larger n, recurse on n/10 and use n%10 for the last digit.

title: Digit detective: backwards
brief: Keep both recursive functions. Add recursive reverseDigits(n,acc) to reverse the decimal digits; leading zeros in the reversed number disappear.
hints: The reverse function needs an accumulator argument.
On each step, do acc=acc*10+n%10 and recurse on n/10.
Stop when n==0; N==0 must also return zero.

title: The service desk
brief: Implement a fixed-size circular queue (capacity 32) and a stack of served ticket numbers. Process A X (enqueue) and S (serve the oldest); report waiting count, served count, and last served ticket (0 if none).
input: K (0–25), then K commands: A X with X=1–999, or S. Every S is valid; total queue size <= 25.
hints: Use an array, front index, and count for the circular queue.
On A, write at (front+count)%32; on S, advance front.
Push every served ticket onto a stack; last is its top.

title: Service desk: undo the last service
brief: Add U to undo the most recently served ticket: pop the served stack and put that ticket back at the FRONT of the circular queue. Also report the next ticket (0 if empty).
input: K (0–25), then K commands: A X, S, or U. Every S/U is valid; total queue size <= 25.

tests.label: Example
tests.input:
7
A 10
A 20
S
A 30
S
U
U

tests.label: Case 3
tests.input:
6
A 4
A 9
S
U
S
S

hints: Undo works in LIFO order using the served stack.
Move front backwards modulo 32, then place the popped ticket there.
Report the next ticket from the queue's front, if present.
